blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: An ejector pump sits in a sealed basin in the basement floor. Basement fixtures below the sewer line, like a toilet, shower, laundry or bar sink, drain into it. When it fills, the pump lifts the wastewater up to the main sewer line. In a home with an [overhead sewer system](/geneva/overhead-sewer-systems), every basement drain depends on it.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Is Your Geneva Ejector Pump Failing?
blocks.intro: Stop using basement fixtures and call if:

tiles.body: The high-water alarm means wastewater is rising in the basin. Stop using basement fixtures until it's checked.
Water backing up in the lowest fixture first is a classic sign the pump isn't emptying the basin.
A loud bang when the pump shuts off often means a worn check valve letting water slam back down.
A failed gasket or a cracked basin can let sewage seep onto the floor.

blocks.intro: Two kinds of Geneva homes rely on ejector pumps the most.

items.h3: Bathrooms Added to Old Stone Basements
items.body: Historic homes near the Fox River often got a basement bathroom decades after they were built. Breaking into an old foundation floor for a basin isn't easy, and some of those installs used pumps that were too small or vented poorly.
More than 4 in 10 Geneva homes were built in 1990 or later, many with a finished lower level and a full bath. In many of those homes, the original ejector pump is now reaching the end.
After storms like September 2008, some homeowners converted to an [overhead sewer system](/geneva/overhead-sewer-systems). In those homes, every basement drain depends on the ejector.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Why does my ejector pump bang when it shuts off?
items.answer: A loud bang or thump when the pump stops usually means the check valve isn't closing smoothly. Replacing it is a common, quick repair.

items.q: Is it safe to use the upstairs bathrooms while the alarm is on?
items.preview: Usually, yes. Upstairs fixtures typically drain by gravity.
items.answer: Usually. In most homes, upstairs fixtures drain directly to the sewer by gravity. Basement fixtures drain to the basin, so stop using those. If you have an overhead sewer, ask us when you call.

items.q: Can a basement bathroom in an old house be upgraded?
items.preview: Yes. We can install a properly sized pump and basin.
items.answer: Yes. If your existing ejector is undersized or poorly vented, we replace it with a pump and basin sized for your fixtures.

items.q: What can go down a toilet connected to an ejector pump?
items.answer: Only toilet paper. Wipes, paper towels and grease clog the pump and shorten its life.

items.q: What does ejector pump replacement cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, basin and access. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin, the check valve and venting and how easy it is to reach. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we open the basin.
